title: ScriptaHub · A library for your curiosity

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Use Suggest An Edit on the book page to propose a correction or extension.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The form helps you identify the book and describe your contribution.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: It prepares an email that you review and send yourself.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You can explain why a change matters and include supporting references.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Useful contributions are considered for the value they add to the work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Major accepted contributions may receive credit.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You do not need to rewrite a whole book to contribute something valuable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: One well-supported correction can give later readers a clearer understanding.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Create is the starting point when you want to propose new work.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You might bring a research direction, an overlooked subject, or a document worth developing.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Explain who would read it and why the subject deserves sustained attention.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: You can also describe the questions a useful book should address.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The proposal form prepares an email for you to review and send.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: If your proposal includes documents, attach them in your email application.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A proposal begins a conversation about the work; it does not guarantee publication.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The aim is to turn a worthwhile idea into something readers can examine.
